newsitem.title: FRANCE: No decision on early close for EU barley sales.
newsitem.headline: No decision on early close for EU barley sales.

text.p: The European Commission has not yet decided whether to extend the halt on weekly soft wheat exports to barley and other grains, but it has not ruled out a date earlier than the May 29 end-of-season, an EU grain source said.
"It's not excluded that we could stop sooner. We will see," the source said.
"The Commission did not accept bids for barley on Thursday so the tender remains in place. But when you're coming to the end (of a July/June season) it's not a big deal when you stop a tender."
The EU on Thursday rejected weekly export bids for all grains and closed the soft wheat tender, originally due to end on May 29.
Officials said the halt was an attempt to rein in domestic prices.
Tenders to export barley, rye, oats, durum wheat and Greek maize from the open market were still theoretically open until May 29.
Similar tenders to export intervention stocks of German rye and barley, and Swedish and Finnish barley, also stay open.
Traders bid for export refunds for open-market eu grain or offer to buy grain from EU intervention stores at fixed prices at weekly tenders each Thursday.
The source said that barring any further changes four such tenders were left until the end of the 1996/97 crop year.
They would be on April 24, May 15, May 22 and May 29. On May 1 and May 8 the Commission will be shut for public holidays. --Paule Bonjean, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
